data.description:
## Description

**What**: Author tests/fixtures/detect-fake.sh + tests/scripts/test-synthetic-detector.sh exercising new tag introduction AND a colliding tag from a non-matching fixture.
**Why**: Demonstrates a third-party detector author can extend the schema using only the published contract, and that collisions deduplicate without errors.
**Scope**:
- IN: Synthetic detector emitting `platform:fake` (new namespaced tag) and `ruby-rails` (compound colliding from a non-Ruby fixture); test asserts (a) `platform:fake` propagates to consumer output, (b) `ruby-rails` is deduplicated to one occurrence in the emitted array, (c) no gate exits non-zero solely due to the collision.
- OUT: Real platform detectors (other epics).

## Done Definitions
- When complete, the synthetic-detector test passes assertions (a), (b), (c) above without modifying any consumer in plugins/dso/scripts/ ← Satisfies: SC4, SC5
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations
- [Testing] Ordering/deduplication contract must be defined in DETECTION-SCHEMA.md
- [Reliability] Collision handling must not silently swallow detector errors — only collision-on-equal-value is benign

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a detector author, synthetic-detector and tag-collision behaviors are verified
